data.title: Quality Gate
data.tagline: A set of conditions that decide whether code may be merged or a release may proceed
data.learningOutcome: Explain a blocked change using its failed metric and agreed threshold, then request a fix and verification.
data.description: All tests may pass while coverage remains below the agreed 80%, keeping a pull request blocked. Checks produce results and the gate evaluates them; branch protection must require that result to enforce the merge restriction.

learning.assumes: Know that code changes can trigger automated checks.
learning.outcome: Explain a blocked change using its failed metric and agreed threshold, then request a fix and verification.

distinctions.label: Feature Flag
distinctions.explanation: Feature Flag dynamically enables or disables features at runtime based on user or tenant identity; Quality Gate uses automated tests during development to stop broken builds before production.

distinctions.label: CI
distinctions.explanation: CI is the automated pipeline workflow that clones repositories and runs test scripts; Quality Gate is the rule set deciding whether results qualify for approval or immediate blocking.

explanation.title: Agree on criteria, then enforce them
explanation.text: Set criteria according to project risk, such as passing critical tests and no severe security findings. CI runs checks; require the gate result in branch protection to block changes that fail.

explanation.title: Use the failure report to choose a fix
explanation.text: For low coverage, inspect untested paths; for failing tests, compare actual and expected results. Rerunning unchanged code or lowering the threshold does not prove that the original problem was fixed.

data.boundary: Passing means the configured criteria were met, not that the software is defect-free. Installing a scanner alone does not block merges; deployment gates must likewise be connected to the release flow.

lessonPractice.title: All 45 PR tests pass, but coverage is 68% against a required 80%. What should happen next?

options.label: Add tests for the uncovered paths, then check the new result
options.feedback: Coverage is the failed condition. Adding tests and verifying again shows whether the agreed criteria are met.

options.label: Rerun the same checks without changing the code or tests
options.feedback: Repeating the same tests does not automatically exercise missing paths.

options.label: Lower the threshold to 60%, then check whether it passes
options.feedback: This changes the admission rule without covering the gap identified in the report.

data.agentPrompt: This PR failed its quality gate. Inspect the report, fix the missing tests or code issue, rerun the checks, and verify that the original gate criteria are satisfied.
